newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan Nov output drop reaction to Oct rise--MITI.
newsitem.headline: Japan Nov output drop reaction to Oct rise--MITI.

text.p: A slight month-on-month fall in Japan's industrial production in November was mainly a reaction to a big rise in the previous month's output, a senior official of the Ministry for International Trade and Industry (MITI) told reporters on Thursday.
The ministry announced that industrial output in November fell 1.9 percent from the previous month.
The official said industrial output is likely to remain firm at least until the end of March.
"The firm trend in industrial production weakened somewhat in November," he said.
The official said it is difficult to predict how a planned rise in the consumption tax in April will affect industrial output.

The tax will be raised from three percent to five percent on April 1. The official said the consumption tax hike has made Japanese manufacturers boost their production plans in the months leading to April.

The ministry announced industrial output in the manufacturing sector is likely to show a month-on-month rise of 5.1 percent in January, of which one-third can be attributed to an expected rise in production ahead of the tax hike.
